milestones.name: The simulation no longer writes a change history every tick, and the sea no longer builds a buffer ladder every frame, for readers that do not exist
milestones.quality_bar: As safe as a dead-code removal in a well-kept engine such as Bevy or wgpu: what goes had no caller, every test of what stays still runs and passes with no expected value edited, and no pixel, state or byte on the wire changes.

items.statement: `thrum-core` keeps no per-tick ring of change bitsets: the ring, the code that maintained it on every write and spawn, its readers and the step that only wrote it are gone. The per-slot change ticks and the structural tick that publication reads are as they were, and the simulation design no longer says the core keeps a change journal.
items.check: sh -c '! git grep -qE "ChangeFrame|invalidate_change_frames|change_ticks3_at" -- crates examples && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-core'
items.ask: Does a write or a spawn still record anything that nothing reads? Did publication, `finalize_activity` or any per-slot tick change? Was any test deleted that covered code that is kept?

items.statement: A world steps to the same state: every test of `thrum-core`, `thrum-sim2d` and `thrum-network` that passed at the starting commit passes, and no expected digest, hash or state in a test was edited.
items.ask: Read the milestone's diff of test files with `git diff` from the commit it started from: is any expected digest, hash, count or state literal changed? Is any test of kept behaviour removed?

items.statement: The sea computes no moment ladder: the moments and mip-parameter buffers, the reduce pipeline, their bind group and records, and the write that fed them are gone, and the sea's graph declares the passes that are left. Water samples the filtered textures as it did. The forward-cache test holds that every mip of the filtered textures carries the moments on all five planes, and water's record test checks no record that nothing binds.
items.check: sh -c '! git grep -qE "moments_buffer|surface_accesses|check_moments" -- crates examples && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-sea -p thrum-water'
items.ask: Does the sea still compute anything each frame that only a test reads? Which test now fails if a filtered-texture mip lost its slope or Jacobian moments, and does it check all five planes of every mip? Did any assertion about the filtered textures or the wave field change?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this milestone moved no retained image.

milestones.name: A scene contribution writes only the hooks it uses
milestones.quality_bar: As safe as a dead-code removal in a well-kept engine such as Bevy or wgpu: what goes had no caller, every test of what stays still runs and passes with no expected value edited, and no pixel, state or byte on the wire changes.

items.statement: `SceneContribution` gives `computes`, `encode_compute`, `encode_after_compute`, `draw` and `submitted` default bodies that do what the empty stubs did, and no implementation under `crates` or `examples` writes a body equal to its default. `passes`, `rebuild` and `encode_upload` stay required. The trait's documentation says that a wrapper must forward every hook, that `encode_compute` is called only when `computes` is true, and that `submitted` commits what `encode_upload` staged.
items.check: sh -c 'git grep -q "trait SceneContribution" -- crates && test "$(git grep -hA1 -E "fn computes\(&self.*\) -> bool \{" -- crates examples | grep -cE "^ *false *$")" -le 1'
items.ask: List every `impl SceneContribution` under `crates` and `examples`: does any still write a body equal to a default, for any of the five hooks? Compare with the starting commit: is any body that did work gone, or any hook's behaviour changed?

items.statement: Each wrapper that stands in front of other contributions, the list, the lent one and the ray-tracing replacement, forwards every hook: a test puts a probe behind each wrapper and sees every hook reach it.
items.ask: For each of the three wrappers, name the test that fails if one hook is not forwarded, and try it: remove one forward in a scratch copy. Does the probe count all eight hooks, the defaulted five among them?

items.statement: Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this milestone moved no retained image.

milestones.name: The engine's public API holds no simulation query, capture, device opener, serialiser or shader copy that only its own tests reach
milestones.quality_bar: As safe as a dead-code removal in a well-kept engine such as Bevy or wgpu: what goes had no caller, every test of what stays still runs and passes with no expected value edited, and no pixel, state or byte on the wire changes.

items.statement: `thrum-core` offers no runtime method, serial transaction visit or incremental capture that only its own tests reached: the seven uncalled runtime methods, the serial visits and `RuntimeDelta` with what served only it are gone. A full capture and undo behave as they did. The property that a visit which refuses a row still refreshes the written row's active bit is held on the chunked visit, with the written column indexed.
items.check: sh -c '! git grep -qE "RuntimeDelta|WorldDelta|restore_through|visit_if_indexed|visit_with_changes|matches_capture" -- crates examples && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-core -p thrum-sim2d -p thrum-network'
items.ask: Read the test that carries the refused-row property now: does it index the written column, run the chunked visit, and fail if the active bit were left stale? Were the capture, restore and undo assertions that used a delta kept, on a full capture? Is any expected digest or state edited?

items.statement: `thrum-render` has one public way to open a device, the device recipe: the three openers that only called each other are gone.
items.check: sh -c '! git grep -qE "fn open_generation(_with_feature_mask|_from)?\(" -- crates examples && git grep -q "fn open_planned_generation" -- crates'

items.statement: The rain model has no serialiser that only a test calls: two preparations of the same bed are compared as values, and two different beds differ. `Tree::bytes`, which the rain cost example uses, is as it was.
items.check: sh -c '! git grep -q "fn to_bytes" -- crates/thrum-rain-model && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-rain-model --test tree'
items.ask: Is the value comparison as strict as the byte comparison was, negative zero in the ground included?

items.statement: The shadowed aerial shader exists once. The test-only copy of the two production pieces is gone, the atmosphere model's test reads the production pieces, and the test that only compared the copy with them is gone. No production shader source changed.
items.check: sh -c 'test -z "$(git ls-files ":(glob)crates/**/synthetic_aerial_shadowed.wgsl")" && git ls-files ":(glob)crates/**/*aerial_camera_shadowed.wgsl" | grep -q . && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-render --lib atmosphere::model'
items.ask: Does `git diff` from the starting commit show any change to a shader file that a pipeline is built from?

milestones.name: The water scene reads its settings in one place, so a proof captures the scene a person opens
milestones.quality_bar: As safe as a dead-code removal in a well-kept engine such as Bevy or wgpu: what goes had no caller, every test of what stays still runs and passes with no expected value edited, and no pixel, state or byte on the wire changes.

items.statement: The water scene's `THRUM_WATER_*` variables and its page query are parsed by one typed settings parse, which the window, the page and the proof tests all use. Where the two parsers disagreed the window's reading stands: a floating scene's heading, `THRUM_WATER_STONE` on only when it is `1`, and `THRUM_WATER_WAKE_BODIES` honoured. A meaning only a test needs has a variable of its own.
items.check: sh -c 'test "$(git grep -lE "var(_os)?\(\"THRUM_WATER_" -- examples | wc -l)" -eq 1 && cargo test --locked --offline -p water-scene --lib'
items.ask: List each setting either parser read at the starting commit, with the reading each gave: does the one parse give the window's reading for every one, and does the log record each decision? Does `scripts/water_cost.py` or `scripts/check_water_browser.mjs` set a variable whose meaning changed?

milestones.name: Bind-group layout entries and graph declarations are each written through one helper
milestones.quality_bar: As safe as a dead-code removal in a well-kept engine such as Bevy or wgpu: what goes had no caller, every test of what stays still runs and passes with no expected value edited, and no pixel, state or byte on the wire changes.

items.statement: `thrum_render::binding` gives a bind-group layout entry for each standard kind: uniform buffer, storage buffer read-only or not, sampled texture, sampler, storage texture and acceleration structure. Outside tests and outside that module, no file under `crates` or `examples` writes a `BindGroupLayoutEntry` literal, except an entry with a count or a dynamic offset, and the local helper sets in the renderer, the asset crate and the clouds are gone. Every layout is what it was.
items.check: sh -c 'git grep -q "pub mod binding" -- crates/thrum-render/src && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-render --lib binding'
items.ask: List every `BindGroupLayoutEntry` literal left outside tests and outside the binding module: does each have a count or a dynamic offset? Pick ten converted entries across five crates and compare each with its literal at the starting commit: same visibility, type, read-only flag, sample type, dimension and minimum size?

items.statement: A graph access that stores with no view is written with `Access::new`, and a graph resource that mirrors a `wgpu` texture is declared from the texture by one function, which declares a 2D texture with the texture's own layers, mips and samples. Every compiled graph is what it was: no graph snapshot was edited.
items.check: sh -c 'git grep -q "fn of_texture" -- crates/thrum-render/src && cargo test --locked --offline -p thrum-render --test graph_kinds'
items.ask: Does the function ever declare a cube or a 3D texture? Read the milestone's diff of snapshot and expected-graph files with `git diff` from the starting commit: is any changed?
